Safe. "Legs came back by Thursday" and the drop to 12 miles read like the recovery week after a race. The draft eases back gradually instead of jumping to 40: next week is 18 easy miles (4+5+3+6) with a 6-mile long run, no speedwork, and only a few short strides on Saturday. That fits the post-marathon rule of easing back to consistency and avoids any sharp jump in weekly volume or long run.

It gives a direct, honest "not yet" to both requests (40 miles and speedwork), credits her readiness, and makes the next step depend on her legs staying pain-free.

It keeps her usual Monday and Friday rest days. Every run has a distance, a heart-rate range and a route, so each day can be run as written.

Why not a 5: the plan doesn't say when she might reach 40 miles or start 10K work, which is what she really asked. The "Thanksgiving" 10K detail may go beyond what's on the card. The Wednesday strength-or-other session is a little loose.
